Total feature width and bit test, set, clear, and zero helper semantics beyond call sites are not shown.
DMA buffer export, attachment, and UUID Oswire contract and error handling beyond validation are not shown.

findings.text: DMA buffer helpers expose export validation plus attach delegation plus identity test plus UUID retrieval for virtio-backed buffers.

Export proceeds only when operations linkage exists and the attach entry matches the virtio handler and a UUID hook is present, otherwise an invalid-argument error pointer results; attach succeeds immediately without a device hook and otherwise propagates that hook outcome; UUID fetch rejects non-virtio buffers before delegating.
Inbound queue helper offers buffer addition for device-originated messages with cache-line debug exemption.

Input device state pairs host and input-core references with three fixed 64-character identity strings, separate event intake and status egress queues, a bounded 64-slot pool for device-originated events isolated for DMA from device, a guard, and a readiness marker.
Event intake replenishes single-element scatter descriptors pointing at caller-provided slots through an inbound helper that requests cache-line debug exemption.

Event reception and status handling hold an interrupt-saving guard while inspecting readiness and draining queues, release it while delivering decoded input onward, then reacquire and revalidate before requeueing and signalling.

Configuration discovery writes a selector pair then reads back a length; capability bitmaps arrive as byte streams with low-bit-first ordering inside each byte and are truncated when the caller asks for more than available; querying event capabilities also records the queried event family as supported.
Absolute axis setup queries per-axis range and resolution plus fuzz and flat values from device configuration and publishes them to the input core.
Input driver registers for the virtio input identifier with no additional feature requests and binds probe, removal, and sleep freeze plus restore handlers.

Probe requires modern version negotiation, allocates driver state, acquires two queues for events and status, copies name and serial with truncation to local capacity, derives a physical path from the device index, populates bus identity with virtual fallback, enumerates properties and key plus relative plus absolute plus miscellaneous plus switch plus LED plus sound capabilities, configures absolute axes and multitouch slots, then marks readiness and registers before prefilling event buffers.

Readiness starts clear, becomes set after device ready and successful registration, returns to clear on registration failure, removal, and freeze, and is set again on successful restore followed by buffer refill.

Status egress suppresses multitouch timestamp echo, allocates its message atomically and reports memory exhaustion on failure, uses little-endian wire order, queues only while ready and otherwise reports absent device, always signals after a queue attempt, and frees the message on queue failure; completion and teardown paths reclaim outstanding status messages.
Sub-block-mode memory blocks use unused, plugged-only, offline full and partial, kernel-zoned full and partial, and movable-zoned full and partial states, with a count sentinel.
Big-block-mode extents use unused, plugged-only, added, and fake-offline prepared for removal, with a count sentinel.

Memory device state holds device linkage, startup unplug need, deferred work plus activity and change counters, one request queue with waiters and single request plus response storage, current and desired sizes, block sizing and placement plus region bounds, resource and group identity, offline accounting with threshold, a mode selector choosing either sub-block tracking with identifiers plus sizes plus state array plus plugged bitmap or big-block tracking with identifiers plus state array plus extent size, plus hotplug guard, health and environment flags, removal guard, retry timing, memory and power notifiers, optional crash-dump capture, and list linkage.
Global device list and online-page callback are guarded by a dedicated mutex; first insertion installs the callback and final removal restores it, with a grace-period wait after list removal.

Per-device hotplug mutex stabilizes block counts, per-block state storage, and sub-block plugged bitmaps against concurrent online and offline transitions and plug activity, and also serializes dump-mode request bookkeeping.

Identifier conversions derive memory-block numbers from address division and reverse by multiplication, derive big-block numbers using the configured extent size, and derive sub-block numbers from offset inside the containing memory block divided by sub-block size.
Two boolean tunables control default onlining behavior and forced big-block mode, with an unsigned long tunable for big-block size override.

Debug inspection enumerates set feature indices one per line for both live device features and the filter mask; clearing with value one empties the filter and any other value leaves it unchanged with success; adding or removing validates the index against total width and rejects overflow.
Default allowance for memory left offline before throttling further addition is one gibibyte.
Retry delay for plug operations spans fifty thousand milliseconds minimum to three hundred thousand milliseconds maximum.
